title: Regulation of the mouse retinal taurine transporter (TAUT) by protein kinases inXenopusoocytes

sections.abstract: <jats:p>The goal was to investigate the role of protein kinases in modulating taurine transporter activity in<jats:italic>Xenopus laevis</jats:italic>oocytes expressing the mouse retinal Na<jats:sup>+</jats:sup>/C<jats:sup>−</jats:sup>/taurine transporter. The currents generated by the taurine transporter were studied with a two‐electrode voltage clamp and we recorded the maximal current (<jats:italic>I</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>max</jats:italic></jats:sub>), presteady‐state charge transfer<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>, and membrane capacitance<jats:italic>C</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>m</jats:italic></jats:sub>. 8‐BR‐cAMP, a membrane‐permeable activator of the cAMP‐dependent protein kinase (PKA), decreased<jats:italic>I</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>max</jats:italic></jats:sub>(41%),<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>(41%) and<jats:italic>C</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>m</jats:italic></jats:sub>(10%). Similarly, 1 μM<jats:italic>sn</jats:italic>‐1,2‐dioctanoylglycerol (DOG), an activator of the Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup><jats:italic>I</jats:italic>diacylglycerol‐dependent protein kinase (PKC), decreased<jats:italic>I</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>max</jats:italic></jats:sub>(56%),<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>(37%), and<jats:italic>C</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>m</jats:italic></jats:sub>(9%). Calyculin A, a specific inhibitor of protein phosphatases 1 and 2A, also produced effects similar to those of 8‐Br‐cAMP and DOG, and decreased<jats:italic>I</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>max</jats:italic></jats:sub>(64%),<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>(38%), and<jats:italic>C</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>m</jats:italic></jats:sub>(10%). We conclude that the taurine transporter is regulated by activators of PKA and PKC, and regulation occurs largely by changes in the number of transporters in the plasma membrane.</jats:p>
